{{Short description|Scottish poet, philosopher, and historian (1829–1894)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
[[File:John Veitch2.jpg|thumb]]
[[File:John Veitch.jpg|thumb|John Veitch]]
'''John Veitch''' (24 October 1829 – 3 September 1894), [[Scotland|Scottish]] [[philosopher]], [[poet]] and [[historian]]: John was born in [[Peebles]]; the only son of [[Peninsular War]] veteran James Veitch and his wife, Nancy Ritchie; a woman, steeped in the folk traditions of the Borders; he was educated at the [[University of Edinburgh]].<ref name=uni>[http://www.universitystory.gla.ac.uk/biography/?id=WH2093&type=P John Veitch]. University of Glasgow</ref>

He was assistant lecturer successively to [[Sir William Hamilton, Bart|Sir William Hamilton]] and [[Alexander Campbell Fraser]] (1856–60). In 1860 he was appointed to the chair of [[logic]], [[metaphysics]] and [[rhetoric]] at the [[University of St Andrews]], and in 1864 to the [[Professor of Logic and Rhetoric|corresponding chair at the University of Glasgow]].<ref name=uni/>

In [[St. Andrews]], he lived at 8 Playfair Terrace.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://fifefhs.org/images/resources/records/parochial-directory/PARISH-OF-ST-ANDREWS.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-11-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171111102117/https://fifefhs.org/images/resources/records/parochial-directory/PARISH-OF-ST-ANDREWS.pdf |archive-date=2017-11-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In [[Glasgow]], he lectured to working men and women and between 1877 and 1883 put on courses for the [[Glasgow Association for the Higher Education of Women]].  He founded the [[Scottish Mountaineering Club]] in 1892.  He deplored the damaging environmental impacts of industrialisation and campaigned to save old buildings.<ref>Cowley, Stephen (1994) ''John Veitch, Scottish Philosopher, Poet and Literary Critic'', in ''Edinburgh Review'' Issue 92, Edinburgh, pp. 141 - 147</ref>

In philosophy an [[intuitionism|intuitionist]], he was dismissive of [[idealism|idealist]] arguments. He is remembered chiefly for his work on the literature and antiquities of the [[Scottish Borders]]. See ''Memoir'' by his niece, Mary RL Bryce (1896).<ref name=uni/>

==Publications==
*Translations of [[René Descartes|Descartes]]' ''Discours de la méthode'' (1850) and ''Méditationes'' (1852)
*An edition of Sir William Hamilton's lectures with memoir (1869, in collaboration with [[Henry Longueville Mansel|HL Mansel]])
*''The Tweed and other Poems'' (1875)<ref>{{cite book|author=John Veitch|title=The Tweed and Other Poems|url=https://archive.org/details/tweedotherpoems00veitrich/page/n8/mode/1up|location=Glasgow|publisher=James Maclehose, publisher to the [[University of Glasgow|University]]; London: [[Macmillan Publishers|Macmillan and Co.]]|oclc=2302595}}</ref>
*''Lucretius and the Atomic Theory'' (1875)
*''The History and Poetry of the Scottish Border'' (1877; ed. 1893)
*''Hamilton'' (1882)
*''The River Tweed from its Source to the Sea'' (1884)
*''Institutes of Logic'' (1885)
*''The Feeling for Nature in Scottish Poetry'' (1887)
*''Knowing and Being'' (1889)
*''Merlin'' (1889)
*''Dualism and Monism'' (1895)
*''Border Essays'' (1896)
